A common report gives each site the same grade in both domains. A profile gives the site a separate grade
for each domain, so it can state A ahead of B in one domain and B ahead of A in the other. The nine profiles
include all three common reports. With the same distribution, weights, and withholding cost, the best
profile can therefore have lower risk. Its two grades describe separate priorities.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Aligned priorities.** Both reports place A ahead of B in both domains. Each has risk 1/10, so the difference is zero.
- **Crossed priorities.** Under equal weights and withholding cost 1/4, the common optimum withholds both
  directions at risk 1/4. The profile reports A ahead in S and B ahead in C at risk 1/10. Allowing that combination
  reduces risk by 3/20 under the same loss.
- **Lower withholding cost.** At cost 1/20, both reports withhold every direction. The risk is 1/20 because
  withholding itself carries a cost.
- **Greater weight on S.** At weights 9/10 and 1/10, the common report follows S and has risk 9/50. The profile
  still states the crossed directions and has risk 1/10. The difference under these weights is 2/25.

With crossed priorities and equal weights, four profiles share the minimum risk of 1/10 at withholding cost
1/10. The app lists all four, including the report that withholds both directions.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The fictional distribution in each example has two states. The calculation evaluates each card under the
same loss, with expected-error and joint caps disabled. A shared grade leaves the direction unstated.
The results apply to the cards considered here.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
The [R script](../../data/recipes/profile-common-vs-domain.R) reproduces all twelve settings with
postrank 1.2.0 and gmp.

```r
source("profile-common-vs-domain.R")
result <- profile_common_vs_domain()
result$summary
```
:::

Source: [postrank multidomain decisions](https://joonho112.github.io/postrank/articles/mdomain-decisions.html).
